title: 6.20.2 Debugging: The wall that falls on its own
description: Two planted bugs. The wall collapses before the first shot, and the last stone never counts.

steps.title: Run it
steps.instructions: The wall is on the ground and it topples before you fire.

steps.title: Bug 1: the stack is unstable
steps.instructions: The bottom block is dynamic with no support, so gravity pulls the stack over. Make the bottom row `static`, or give every block `rotationLock = true`.

steps.title: Bug 2: the last stone is ignored
steps.instructions: The win and lose check runs before the sweep clears the last stone, so "out of shots" waits a frame too long. Move the sweep above the check.
hints: The order in `draw()` is the bug: cleanup, then decide.

requirements.title: The stack holds
requirements.description: The bottom row is static, or blocks have rotationLock. Help: 6.19.1 (Reading: Blocks that fall)

requirements.title: Cleanup before the check
requirements.description: The shot sweep runs before the win/lose test. Help: 6.20.1 (Lab: Five shots, win or lose)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch for "Debugging: The wall that falls on its own". The task: stabilise the block stack so it does not fall on its own, and clear spent shots before deciding win or lose. Accept any names, helpers, ternaries and semicolons; a line only in a comment or string does not count. Short, plain notes for a 14-year-old; never write corrected code.

rubric.title: Order
rubric.description: The sweep comes before the end check.
